references.text: Continuation of the same law regarding disputes over property, where God (אֱלֹהִים) decides the case between the parties.
Difficult legal cases shall be brought to the judges and priests who serve before the Lord, paralleling bringing the case 'to God' (הָאֱלֹהִים).
Two men who have a dispute shall stand before the Lord, before the priests and judges, following similar procedures for legal judgments.
The use of אֱלֹהִים in a legal context, where the master is to bring the servant before God/the judges.
God stands in the divine assembly and judges among 'the gods' (אֱלֹהִים), referring to judges who represent God's authority.
The principle of double restitution (שְׁנַיִם) is also mentioned here regarding theft of livestock.
The previous verse deals with the same type of case concerning entrusted property and double restitution in cases of theft.
Laws concerning fraudulent handling of entrusted property and restitution, a parallel theme regarding פֶּשַׁע (transgression) concerning property.
Complementary laws on restitution: Exodus sets penalties by judgment (double), while Leviticus regulates voluntary restoration with an added portion.
Theological parallel: Affirmation of the requirement for full restitution plus a fifth part upon acknowledgment of guilt for unjust appropriation.
Complementary aspects of sin: Economic restoration to the person (Exodus) combined with ritual atonement to God (Leviticus).
Connected legal text: Rules for full restitution in cases of obvious theft (22:2) and double payment by judgment in embezzlement cases (22:8).
Direct definition: Leviticus 5:23 defines the specific acts (entrusted/lost) for which Exodus 22:8 requires judgment and restitution.
